_comment: Grounding regression fixture for bin/fleet_eval_grounding.py.
Every probe here is a question the fleet was actually asked and got wrong, or the
control that proves the retrieval path works at all. Adding a probe is an edit to
this file; the runner carries no query text.
WHY THIS EXISTS. On 2026-08-11 Claudius was asked about the live approval pipeline,
queried the vault correctly, and answered by quoting a decision from 2026-07-09.
Nothing malfunctioned — the vault had never been told about the Buzz migration,
because Praetorium holds no canonical vault credential and box-side work only
reaches the vault when Dave promotes it from the Mac. Retrieval ranks on wording,
not on age, and a superseded document does not announce that it is superseded.
PATH SPELLING. `index` is qmd's spelling (hyphens), `disk` is the on-disk spelling
(underscores). They genuinely differ and retyping one in the other's dialect returns
`No files matched pattern`, which is indistinguishable from the document not
existing. Both are stated so the runner can assert both resolve.
BASELINE. Each probe records the verdict measured when it was added, so the gate
fires on REGRESSION rather than on a state that was already known and accepted.
PASS > POINTER > FAIL. A probe that beats its baseline is reported as an
improvement and the baseline is left alone — bumping it is a deliberate edit, not
something a scheduled job does to its own fixture.
PROBE SHAPE. A probe without `must_answer` asserts a document — did the anchor
rank within `max_rank`, and if not, does the winner's span point at it. A probe
WITH `must_answer` asserts the anchor's own retrieved span: PASS when the span
matches, POINTER when the anchor ranks but its span no longer carries the answer,
FAIL when the anchor drops out of `max_rank` entirely. Both shapes score against
the same PASS > POINTER > FAIL ladder.
Documents on disk that qmd's walker never picked up. Four vendored skill files
under 08_skills/vp-pitch-deck/vendor/ have sat unindexed since 2026-07-27 — they
are plain files, not symlinks, and every other document in that tree is indexed, so
this is the walker's own rule rather than a stale index. Baselined at 4 so the
count stays quiet and the fifth one — a document no agent could ever retrieve —
shows up. Dot-directories are excluded before counting; qmd indexes none of them.
The load-bearing mechanism. Retrieval is best-effort; this layer is present on
every turn regardless of what `query` ranks first, so its loss is a hard failure
even on a day when all three probes pass.
team_instructions.section: A lookup can also come back full, confident, and a month out of date

_comment: Trend, not gate. The count of documents in the project folder that never mention
the anchor topic — 10 on 2026-08-11. Each one is a document that reads as current
and describes the retired Discord/Hermes/Kanban design. Recorded so the number is
visibly going down instead of being rediscovered.

probes.why: Control. Phrased in Buzz-native terms, so retrieval alone should find the anchor. If this one fails the index is broken, not the wording.

searches.query: which channel does a scheduled job publish its report to, and what event kind does it need?

probes.why: The plainly-worded version of the same question. On 2026-08-11 this returned agent-inbox-sync/SKILL.md first and the anchor fourth at 0.44; after two supersession banners were added it returned inbox_workflow.md first, which mentions Buzz nowhere at all. Bannering two documents promoted an unbannered third.

searches.query: how does the agent workforce publish its work and get proposals approved today?

probes.why: Claudius's exact failure. The top hit carried a supersession banner at lines 6-10 and the retrieved span was line 85 — the pointer existed and was outside the window the agent saw. This probe is the reason the span, not the document, is what gets checked.

searches.query: are we still building the NUC implementation cards, and what was decided about the approval gate?
NUC-25b approval gate decision Notion inbox status

probes.why: The placement guard. The other three probes assert which document wins; this one asserts that the anchor's own retrieved span still contains the answer, because those are different failures. A document is represented in results by ONE chunk, so prose added anywhere above re-cuts every boundary below it and the chunk that used to answer stops existing while the file keeps ranking first. Measured 2026-08-11: a six-line section inserted at the top of the anchor knocked p1_route_kind from rank 1 to rank 3, and only luck made that visible — a smaller shift would have kept rank 1 and quietly handed the agent a window with no answer in it. The answer chosen is the forum root-post kind, `45001`, because it is a single token that is either in the window or is not, and because sending kind 9 into a forum is the exact mistake this vault section exists to prevent (buzz_architecture §3). Measured PASS on the live index: anchor rank 1, span `@@ -44,4 @@`, deterministic over three runs.

searches.query: what event kind does a root post in a forum channel need?
forum root post event kind stream
